title: HD20-4000 Series IoT Controller | 4DO, 4DI & 4AI | Hitelecom
metaDescription: HD20-4000 IoT controller with 4DO + 4DI + 4AI reference I/O, edge acquisition, local, remote and condition-based control, watchdogs and Hitelecom Cloud monitoring.
heroValue:
Connect field signals.
Control with context.
heroDescription: The Hitelecom HD20-4000 series combines field data acquisition, equipment monitoring and control in a compact RTU. The 4DO + 4DI + 4AI reference configuration connects digital equipment states, external analogue measurements and compatible control circuits. Edge processing, local, remote and condition-based control, and remote configuration and firmware upgrades support the installation throughout its operating life. View uploaded monitoring data online in Hitelecom Cloud and receive alerts when configured thresholds are exceeded.
reviewNotice: Reference configuration: 4 digital outputs, 4 digital inputs and 4 analogue inputs. Select electrical signal types, load interfaces, communication settings and installation requirements for the ordered version.

interfaceCards.title: Digital outputs
interfaceCards.text: Issue defined control commands through four digital outputs in the reference configuration. Select the output electrical type and connect each point to a compatible equipment control circuit.

interfaceCards.title: Digital inputs
interfaceCards.text: Acquire four equipment-state signals in the reference configuration. Define the electrical compatibility, normal state and operating meaning of each digital input.

interfaceCards.title: Analogue inputs
interfaceCards.text: Acquire four analogue measurement signals in the reference configuration. Match each external transmitter to the supplied input range, engineering units and scaling.

features.title: Digital and analogue I/O together
features.text: The 4DO + 4DI + 4AI reference configuration combines four control outputs, four equipment-state inputs and four analogue measurement inputs. Build the point allocation around the actual instrument and equipment signal list.

features.title: Edge processing at the equipment
features.text: Process field information close to its source for equipment monitoring and condition-based actions. The project configuration defines the signal interpretation, control conditions and permitted responses.

features.title: Local, remote and condition-based control
features.text: Use the operating mode that fits the task: local operation, remote supervision or an action linked to a configured condition. Define priorities and equipment feedback for the selected control arrangement.

features.title: Master/slave operating modes
features.text: Support project-defined device coordination with master/slave working modes. The selected interface, communication protocol and device roles form part of the integration configuration.

features.title: Online monitoring and threshold alerts
features.text: Use Hitelecom Cloud to view uploaded monitoring data online and receive alerts when configured thresholds are exceeded. Map equipment states, measurement units and alert recipients to the operating workflow.

features.title: Remote configuration and upgrades
features.text: Adjust supported settings and upgrade device firmware remotely. Plan maintenance around the installed configuration, software version and the site’s operating procedure.

features.title: Hardware and software watchdogs
features.text: Dual watchdog mechanisms support recovery from defined software or system faults. Recovery behaviour and output states are part of the device configuration and commissioning checks.

features.title: Compact integration for field equipment
features.text: Bring monitoring and control into equipment rooms, service cabinets and distributed installations with a compact controller design. Select the power, enclosure and wiring arrangement for the site.

workflow.title: Acquire the field signals
workflow.text: Connect equipment-state signals and compatible analogue transmitter outputs. Give each point an asset identity, signal definition, engineering range and normal state.

workflow.title: Apply the operating logic
workflow.text: Select local, remote or condition-based operation for each permitted action. Specify the initiating condition, command priority and equipment response required by the project.

workflow.title: Issue the permitted action
workflow.text: Send defined digital commands through electrically compatible control interfaces. The host equipment retains its sequencing, interlocks and independent protection functions.

workflow.title: Observe and verify the result
workflow.text: Check available equipment feedback independently of the output command. View uploaded states and measurements in Hitelecom Cloud and verify configured threshold alerts during commissioning.

applicationsIntro: Eight application areas, with five engineering tasks in each, show how the controller can connect monitoring points and permitted control actions. These 40 tasks are selection examples, not 40 simultaneous channels or a claim that every task is fitted in one device. Allocate the selected signals against the 4DI / 4AI / 4DO reference configuration; larger point lists may require another configuration or additional controllers. External instruments, communication interfaces and load-control equipment are selected for the project.

groups.title: Vending & Self-Service Equipment
groups.intro: Connect selected machine states, external measurements and auxiliary control circuits for service visibility across unattended retail equipment. Define the interface with the machine supplier; dispensing sequences, payment and transaction processing remain with their dedicated systems.

tasks.title: Machine availability and service faults
tasks.text: Read available ready, running or fault signals to distinguish a machine that is available for service from one requiring inspection.
tasks.interface: Allocate compatible DI points to the selected machine-state outputs.
tasks.control: Use a DO only for an auxiliary command expressly supported by the machine’s external interface.
tasks.verification: Check every state against the machine display and source signal; connectivity alone does not establish machine availability.

tasks.control: Configure threshold alerts; any supervisory enable request must use the refrigeration unit’s approved interface.
tasks.verification: Compare readings with the source instruments and verify the complete alert workflow; refrigeration protection remains with the unit.

tasks.title: Service-door and access events

tasks.verification: Check normal-state logic and planned maintenance events; an access event does not by itself identify or authorize a person.

tasks.title: Auxiliary lighting and service indication

tasks.control: Use the agreed local, remote or condition-based operating priority.
tasks.verification: Verify the actual lamp or indicator response and local override; keep the vending and payment controller’s functions separate.

faqs.q: What is the HD20-4000 series designed to do?
faqs.a: It combines field data acquisition, equipment monitoring and control in an IoT RTU. Digital inputs capture equipment states, analogue inputs receive compatible transmitter signals, and digital outputs connect to permitted control circuits. Edge processing, cloud monitoring and remote maintenance support the operating workflow.

The reference arrangement is 4DO + 4DI + 4AI: four digital outputs, four digital inputs and four analogue inputs. The series supports project-selected I/O arrangements. Confirm the channel allocation and obtain the electrical specification for the ordered version. The 40 application tasks are selection examples, not 40 simultaneous channels; a larger point list may need another configuration or additional controllers.

faqs.q: Which signals can the digital and analogue inputs accept?
faqs.a: DI points acquire compatible digital equipment states; AI points acquire compatible analogue transmitter outputs. Match electrical logic, signal ranges, isolation and accuracy conditions to the selected version and external instrument. Provide the instrument output specification during selection. A DO, DI or AI label alone does not establish a relay topology, a voltage/current range or a communication protocol.

The series supports local, remote and condition-based control. For each action, define the triggering condition, command priority, permitted operating scope and available feedback. Connect outputs through electrically compatible control interfaces. The host equipment retains its sequence, interlocks and independent protection functions.

faqs.q: What do master/slave operating modes mean for integration?
faqs.a: These are working roles for project-defined device coordination. Identify which device initiates an exchange, which responds, and the data or commands involved. Select the actual interface, communication protocol and supported operations for the project. The master/slave description by itself does not establish a serial port type or a particular protocol.

faqs.q: Can I view monitoring data and receive alerts in Hitelecom Cloud?
faqs.a: Yes. Hitelecom Cloud supports online viewing of uploaded monitoring data and alerts when configured thresholds are exceeded. Configure the measurement units, equipment-state meanings, limits and notification workflow for the connected points. Data availability and notification timing depend on the device reporting profile and network connection.

faqs.q: Can the controller be integrated with a customer platform?
faqs.a: Customer-platform, PLC, machine and shelf-system integration is reviewed against the interfaces supported by the selected configuration. Agree the physical connection, protocol where applicable, point definitions, permitted commands and equipment-feedback mapping. Connection to an auxiliary signal does not establish native compatibility with a machine, electronic shelf-label network or payment system.

faqs.q: What is the purpose of the two watchdog mechanisms?
faqs.a: The series uses hardware and software watchdog mechanisms to support recovery from defined faults. They are device-recovery features, not a guarantee of uninterrupted operation or a replacement for equipment protection. Commissioning should verify the applicable reset behaviour and the resulting output states.

faqs.q: Can settings and firmware be maintained remotely?
faqs.a: The series supports remote configuration and remote firmware upgrades. Use the settings and firmware intended for the delivered hardware configuration, and plan maintenance around the site operating procedure. Verify the required settings and device operation after the change.

faqs.q: What happens when communication or power is interrupted?
faqs.a: Local and condition-based control are supported operating modes, but lost-link operation, output fallback states and start-up recovery must be specified for the delivered configuration. A remote command path and an online monitoring view depend on connectivity. Test the agreed interruption and recovery behaviour at commissioning.

faqs.q: Can a digital output directly power a pump, fan or valve?
faqs.a: Select the connection using the output electrical type, the permitted load and the equipment interface. A suitable starter, contactor, intermediate switching device or actuator control circuit may be required. Output activation alone does not prove that a motor is running or a valve has reached position; use available equipment feedback.

faqs.q: What information is needed to select an installation configuration?
faqs.a: Provide the installation country, signal list, instrument output specifications, equipment-control interfaces, required local/remote priorities, power source and site conditions. Include the target platform and the expected behaviour during communication loss or restart. These details establish the I/O allocation, integration scope and any customization requirements.

enquiryIntro: Share the instrument outputs, equipment-state points, permitted commands and feedback required at the site. We will review the 4DO + 4DI + 4AI reference allocation against the signal list, define local and remote priorities, and scope Hitelecom Cloud or customer-platform integration.
